summary: Long-lived gRPC streams disconnect after ~30m when customer egress proxy initiates TLS renegotiation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-lived gRPC streaming sessions (chat/generation routes) on their Private deployment reliably drop after ~30 minutes. Sessions terminate with application-level errors (gRPC INTERNAL / UNAVAILABLE) even though pod health and CPU/memory are normal.

Impact:
Multiple production customers behind the same egress appliance (FinLedger) experience intermittent stream failures that interrupt in-progress conversations and chunked streaming responses. Severity is high because sessions are stateful and user-facing.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment in customer's VPC (FinLedger)
- Prod, us-east-1 region
- Corporate outbound proxy (BlueBox Inspect 3.2) doing TLS interception and outbound filtering
- Serving nodes use BoringSSL-based runtime (Redwood serving-runtime v2.13.1)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long-lived gRPC streaming session via the customer's app (server-side streaming generation).
2) Stream is stable for ~30 minutes.
3) At ~30 minute mark, stream abruptly terminates with error on client: "rpc error: code = Internal desc = stream terminated" or similar.
4) Server logs around the time show TLS handshake/alert messages and connection close.

Observed logs / captures provided by customer: (snippets)
- serving-runtime: "ERROR tls_handshake: unexpected message during handshake, closing connection"
- kernel net logs: repeated FIN from client side following TLS alert
- tcpdump on egress: a TLS ClientHello labeled as "renegotiation" from the corporate proxy at t+00:30:12

Expected behaviour:
Long-lived streams should remain open barring explicit client/server close or network loss. TLS interception should not cause application-level connection termination.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Configure application-level keepalives to close and re-open streams before 25 minutes as a mitigation (client change).
- Configure egress device to operate in TLS passthrough mode for Redwood endpoints (recommended) to avoid interception.

Permanent remediation (under investigation):
- Customer to change egress proxy policy to disable TLS renegotiation or not perform active rekeying on in-flight connections.
- Engineering to add clearer failure type detection and automatic retry with backoff at the streaming layer; follow-up PR opened.

Attachments/References:
- PCAP supplied by customer (s3 link in customer ticket)
- Slack thread: #support-private-deploy (link: slack://channel?team=redwood&id=C12345)
- Serving runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4587
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
2026-03-12 09:15 UTC - Customer opened ticket after multiple incidents of mid-conversation drops.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Support reproduced issue in customer's staging mirror using their BlueBox appliance configuration. Connection stable until ~30m then dropped.
2026-03-12 13:30 UTC - Packet capture review: outbound egress device issues a TLS renegotiation ClientHello mid-connection. Serving node responds with fatal alert (handshake_failure) and tear-down.
2026-03-13 08:00 UTC - Confirmed runtime uses BoringSSL where renegotiation is disabled by default for security reasons; library returns fatal/NO_RENEGOTIATION alert when peer requests renegotiation.
2026-03-13 12:45 UTC - Reproduced with mitmproxy configured for on-the-fly rekeying; behavior matches customer capture.

Hypothesis:
- The corporate egress proxy attempts to rekey or perform an inspection-triggered renegotiation mid-stream. BoringSSL in serving-runtime rejects renegotiation (security-disabled), causing the server to abort the connection, which surfaces as gRPC INTERNAL/UNAVAILABLE.

Actions taken so far:
- Shared pcap and log excerpts with customer network team.
- Recommended immediate mitigations (passthrough, client keepalive change).
- Opened internal PR to make streaming layer detect fatal TLS alert with clearer error and perform automatic re-open/retry (non-destructive) for idempotent endpoints. PR link in related_github_prs.
- Raised postmortem follow-up to evaluate adding a runtime knob to accept TLS renegotiation only when explicitly configured (security review required).

Next steps:
- Coordinate with FinLedger network team to disable renegotiation for Redwood endpoints; customer has scheduled a maintenance window 2026-03-15.
- Engineering to land enhanced retry behavior for streaming endpoints (PR under review, target 2026-03-20).
- Draft runbook entry for Support and SRE that covers detecting TLS renegotiation events and applying the passthrough workaround.
